lines.text: Tomorrow, dogs everywhere will take one look at the rain and decide they can hold it.
Right now, tomorrow's rain is ruining someone else's evening.
Somewhere tonight, a wedding planner is rehearsing 'rain is good luck.'
Tomorrow, the umbrella hats come out. All three of them.
Tomorrow, everyone in glasses will wish they came with tiny wipers.
Umbrellas haven't had an update in centuries. It shows.
Someone from somewhere colder will say 'you call this cold?' while zipping up.
'There's no bad weather, only bad clothing,' say people who own a lot of fleece.
Tomorrow, the cold-plunge crowd gets a free session.
Tomorrow, a lot of cold hands will end up on warm necks. Uninvited.
Tech billionaires call that a philosophy.
I pitched an afternoon costume change. The weather wouldn't budge.
One drawing for the whole day. Galleries charge admission for less.
Tomorrow the weather's taking the day off. I still have to come in and announce it.
Weather apps will still send three notifications about it.
Someone should check on the weather. This isn't like it.
